audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 11, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for siege setting, royal surveillance, Bathsheba's identity and washing, 'sent and took' coercion, pregnancy, attempted reproductive cover-up, intoxication, Uriah's loyalty, murder order, collateral deaths, command responsibility, mourning, and palace seizure.

verses.restored: At return of year, at time kings go out, David sent Joab, his servants with him, and all Israel. They ruined children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah, but David remained in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.

modern.text: In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and his servants with the whole army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah, but David remained in Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ לִתְשׁוּבַ֨ת הַשָּׁנָ֜ה לְעֵ֣ת צֵ֣את הַמַּלְאֿכִ֗ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח דָּוִ֡ד אֶת יוֹאָב֩ וְאֶת עֲבָדָ֨יו עִמּ֜וֹ וְאֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיַּשְׁחִ֨תוּ֙ אֶת בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עַל רַבָּ֑ה וְדָוִ֖ד יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: At evening David arose from his bed and walked upon roof of house of king. From roof he saw a woman bathing, and woman was very good in appearance.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.

modern.text: One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing—a very beautiful woman.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י לְעֵ֣ת הָעֶ֗רֶב וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד מֵעַ֤ל מִשְׁכָּבוֹ֙ וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ֙ עַל גַּ֣ג בֵּית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אִשָּׁ֛ה רֹחֶ֖צֶת מֵעַ֣ל הַגָּ֑ג וְהָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: David sent and inquired concerning woman. One said, Is this not Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?

familiar.text: And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?

modern.text: So David sent and inquired about the woman, and he was told, “This is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּדְרֹ֖שׁ לָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲלוֹא זֹאת֙ בַּת שֶׁ֣בַע בַּת אֱלִיעָ֔ם אֵ֖שֶׁת אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּֽי

verses.restored: David sent messengers and took her. She came to him, and he lay with her. She was cleansing herself from her impurity, and she returned to her house.

familiar.text: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.

modern.text: Then David sent messengers to get her, and when she came to him, he slept with her. (Now she had just purified herself from her uncleanness.) Then she returned home.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד מַלְאָכִ֜ים וַיִּקָּחֶ֗הָ וַתָּב֤וֹא אֵלָיו֙ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמָּ֔הּ וְהִ֥יא מִתְקַדֶּ֖שֶׁת מִטֻּמְאָתָ֑הּ וַתָּ֖שָׁב אֶל בֵּיתָֽהּ

verses.restored: Woman conceived. She sent and told David, and said, I am pregnant.

familiar.text: And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.

modern.text: And the woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”

original.text: וַתַּ֖הַר הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתִּשְׁלַח֙ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֔ד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הָרָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: David sent to Joab, saying, Send Uriah the Hittite to me. Joab sent Uriah to David.

familiar.text: And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.

modern.text: At this, David sent orders to Joab: “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” So Joab sent him to David.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ אֶל יוֹאָ֔ב שְׁלַ֣ח אֵלַ֔י אֶת אֽוּרִיָּ֖ה הַחִתִּ֑י וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת אֽוּרִיָּ֖ה אֶל דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Uriah came to him. David asked concerning peace of Joab, peace of people, and peace of war.

familiar.text: And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.

modern.text: When Uriah came to him, David asked how Joab and the troops were doing with the war.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אוּרִיָּ֖ה אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל דָּוִ֗ד לִשְׁל֤וֹם יוֹאָב֙ וְלִשְׁל֣וֹם הָעָ֔ם וְלִשְׁל֖וֹם הַמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: David said to Uriah, Go down to your house and wash your feet. Uriah went out from house of king, and a gift/portion from king went out after him.

familiar.text: And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there followed him a mess of meat from the king.

modern.text: Then he said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” So Uriah left the palace, and a gift from the king followed him.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ לְא֣וּרִיָּ֔ה רֵ֥ד לְבֵיתְךָ֖ וּרְחַ֣ץ רַגְלֶ֑יךָ וַיֵּצֵ֤א אֽוּרִיָּה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתֵּצֵ֥א אַחֲרָ֖יו מַשְׂאַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Uriah lay at entrance of house of king with all servants of his lord and did not go down to his house.

familiar.text: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.

modern.text: But Uriah slept at the door of the palace with all his master’s servants; he did not go down to his house.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב אוּרִיָּ֗ה פֶּ֚תַח בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל עַבְדֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָרַ֖ד אֶל בֵּיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: They told David, saying, Uriah did not go down to his house. David said to Uriah, Did you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?

familiar.text: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from thy journey? why then didst thou not go down unto thine house?

modern.text: And David was told, “Uriah did not go home.” “Haven’t you just arrived from a journey?” David asked Uriah. “Why didn’t you go home?”

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא יָרַ֥ד אוּרִיָּ֖ה אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל אוּרִיָּ֗ה הֲל֤וֹא מִדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אַתָּ֣ה בָ֔א מַדּ֖וּעַ לֹֽא יָרַ֥דְתָּ אֶל בֵּיתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Uriah said to David, Ark, Israel, and Judah dwell in shelters; my lord Joab and servants of my lord camp upon face of field. Shall I go to my house to eat, drink, and lie with my wife? By your life and life of your soul, I will not do this thing.

familiar.text: And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.

modern.text: Uriah answered, “The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, and my master Joab and his soldiers are camped in the open field. How can I go to my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אוּרִיָּ֜ה אֶל דָּוִ֗ד הָ֠אָרוֹן וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וִֽיהוּדָ֜ה יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בַּסֻּכּ֗וֹת וַאדֹנִ֨י יוֹאָ֜ב וְעַבְדֵ֤י אֲדֹנִ֨י עַל פְּנֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ חֹנִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֞י אָב֧וֹא אֶל בֵּיתִ֛י לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת וְלִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִם אִשְׁתִּ֑י חַיֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְחֵ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ אִֽם אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: David said to Uriah, Stay here also today, and tomorrow I will send you. Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and next.

familiar.text: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.

modern.text: “Stay here one more day,” David said to Uriah, “and tomorrow I will send you back.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל אוּרִיָּ֗ה שֵׁ֥ב בָּזֶ֛ה גַּם הַיּ֖וֹם וּמָחָ֣ר אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב אוּרִיָּ֧ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וּמִֽמָּחֳרָֽת

verses.restored: David called him, and he ate and drank before him. David made him drunk. In evening he went out to lie on his bed with servants of his lord, but he did not go down to his house.

familiar.text: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.

modern.text: Then David invited Uriah to eat and drink with him, and he got Uriah drunk. And in the evening Uriah went out to lie down on his cot with his master’s servants, but he did not go home. David Arranges Uriah’s Death

original.text: וַיִּקְרָא ל֣וֹ דָוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֧אכַל לְפָנָ֛יו וַיֵּ֖שְׁתְּ וַֽיְשַׁכְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיֵּצֵ֣א בָעֶ֗רֶב לִשְׁכַּ֤ב בְּמִשְׁכָּבוֹ֙ עִם עַבְדֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔יו וְאֶל בֵּית֖וֹ לֹ֥א יָרָֽד

verses.restored: In morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by hand of Uriah.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

modern.text: The next morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּכְתֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד סֵ֖פֶר אֶל יוֹאָ֑ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח בְּיַ֥ד אוּרִיָּֽה

verses.restored: He wrote in letter, saying, Place Uriah at front of fiercest battle and turn back from behind him, so he may be struck and die.

familiar.text: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.

modern.text: In the letter he wrote: “Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle; then withdraw from him, so that he may be struck down and killed.”

original.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֥ב בַּסֵּ֖פֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר הָב֣וּ אֶת אֽוּרִיָּ֗ה אֶל מוּל֙ פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הַֽחֲזָקָ֔ה וְשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם מֵאַחֲרָ֖יו וְנִכָּ֥ה וָמֵֽת

verses.restored: When Joab watched city, he assigned Uriah to place where he knew strong warriors were.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men were.

modern.text: So as Joab besieged the city, he assigned Uriah to a place where he saw the strongest enemy soldiers.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י בִּשְׁמ֥וֹר יוֹאָ֖ב אֶל הָעִ֑יר וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת א֣וּרִיָּ֔ה אֶל הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י אַנְשֵׁי חַ֖יִל שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Men of city went out and fought with Joab. Some of people, from servants of David, fell; Uriah the Hittite also died.

familiar.text: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

modern.text: And when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of David’s servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ וַיִּלָּחֲמ֣וּ אֶת יוֹאָ֔ב וַיִּפֹּ֥ל מִן הָעָ֖ם מֵעַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיָּ֕מָת גַּ֖ם אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּֽי

verses.restored: Joab sent and told David all matters of war.

familiar.text: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

modern.text: Joab sent to David a full account of the battle

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח יוֹאָ֑ב וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֔ד אֶת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֖י הַמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: He commanded messenger, saying, When you finish speaking all matters of war to king,

familiar.text: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,

modern.text: and instructed the messenger, “When you have finished giving the king all the details of the battle,

original.text: וַיְצַ֥ו אֶת הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּכַלּוֹתְךָ֗ אֵ֛ת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: if anger of king rises and he says, Why did you approach so near city to fight? Did you not know they would shoot from wall?

familiar.text: And if so be that the king’s wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?

modern.text: if the king’s anger flares, he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Did you not realize they would shoot from atop the wall?

original.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אִֽם תַּעֲלֶה֙ חֲמַ֣ת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאָמַ֣ר לְךָ֔ מַדּ֛וּעַ נִגַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֶל הָעִ֖יר לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם הֲל֣וֹא יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר יֹר֖וּ מֵעַ֥ל הַחוֹמָֽה

verses.restored: Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman throw upper millstone upon him from wall so he died at Thebez? Why did you approach wall? Then say, Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.

familiar.text: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

modern.text: Who was the one to strike Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth ? Was it not a woman who dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?’ If so, then you are to say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.’”

original.text: מִֽי הִכָּ֞ה אֶת אֲבִימֶ֣לֶךְ בֶּן יְרֻבֶּ֗שֶׁת הֲלֽוֹא אִשָּׁ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יכָה עָלָיו֩ פֶּ֨לַח רֶ֜כֶב מֵעַ֤ל הַֽחוֹמָה֙ וַיָּ֣מָת בְּתֵבֵ֔ץ לָ֥מָּה נִגַּשְׁתֶּ֖ם אֶל הַֽחוֹמָ֑ה וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ גַּ֗ם עַבְדְּךָ֛ אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּ֖י מֵֽת

verses.restored: Messenger went, came, and told David all that Joab had sent him to tell.

familiar.text: So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.

modern.text: So the messenger set out and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to say.

original.text: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הַמַּלְאָ֑ךְ וַיָּבֹא֙ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֔ד אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁלָח֖וֹ יוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: Messenger said to David, Men were strong against us and came out to us into field, but we pressed them as far as entrance of gate.

familiar.text: And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.

modern.text: The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and came out against us in the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד כִּֽי גָבְר֤וּ עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיֵּצְא֥וּ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַנִּהְיֶ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עַד פֶּ֥תַח הַשָּֽׁעַר

verses.restored: Shooters shot at your servants from wall. Some servants of king died, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.

familiar.text: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king’s servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

modern.text: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s servants were killed. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.”

original.text: ויראו המוראים אֶל עֲבָדֶ֨ךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַחוֹמָ֔ה וַיָּמ֖וּתוּ מֵעַבְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְגַ֗ם עַבְדְּךָ֛ אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּ֖י מֵֽת

translation_notes: Bathsheba is named before the encounter as daughter of Eliam and wife of Uriah. Her relationships and personhood precede David's desire.

The Hebrew sequence says David 'sent' and 'took' her. A king with messengers, palace power, and authority over her husband creates coercion; the text records no request from David and no consent from Bathsheba.
Her ritual washing is not seduction. The rooftop viewpoint belongs to David; she is not blamed for being seen.
Her message 'I am pregnant' is the chapter's clearest direct speech and exposes consequences that royal power tries to conceal.
David attempts reproductive cover-up by ordering Uriah home, then uses alcohol when the first plan fails. Intoxication is an instrument of coercion here.
Uriah is a Hittite and a loyal soldier; ethnicity does not make him less part of Israel or less worthy of justice.

David sends Uriah carrying his own death order and engineers battlefield abandonment. Joab executes the plan, and additional soldiers die. This is murder through command authority and collateral killing.
'The sword devours one and another' is David's euphemism for a death he arranged. Fatalism must not erase command responsibility.
Bathsheba's mourning is centered. Palace marriage after the murder does not retroactively create consent or repair the abuse.
safety_note: Maximum survivor-centered safeguards: This chapter depicts royal sexual abuse, reproductive coercion, intoxication, cover-up, murder, and war-command abuse. Do not call Bathsheba a temptress or adulteress, speculate that she invited David's gaze, or use later marriage to erase coercion. David's spiritual importance never exempts him from accountability.
